newsitem.title: GERMANY: German jobless target still achievable - Jagoda.
newsitem.headline: German jobless target still achievable - Jagoda.

text.p: Federal Labour Office chief Bernhard Jagoda said on Tuesday that it was still possible for Germany to hit a government target of 4.2 million unemployed on average this year.

"I believe that if people make an effort for Germany that the 4.2 million figure contained in the federal government statistics is possible," Jagoda told reporters after the publication of March jobless figures.
German jobless target still achievable - Jagoda

But Jagoda cautioned that it was still early to give a proper forecast for unemployment this year. "We have a difficult first quarter behind us, but I can't say after three months whether we will reach 4.2 million," he said.

Unadjusted unemployment -- the most politically sensitive jobs number in Germany -- fell in March to 4.48 million from 4.67 in February, which was the highest since 1933. The seasonally-adjusted figure fell by 15,000 to 4.30 million.

The German government has based its plan to cut borrowing this year to meet the Maastricht treaty budget deficit goal of three percent of GDP, and thereby qualify for Europe's single currency, on a view that joblessness will average 4.2 million.
